Central automatic drilling
Computer and data

stem: Which device is fitted to an elephant so that rangers can follow its movements?

options.content: A GPS tracking collar
options.rationale: Correct: it sends the animal's position regularly.

options.content: A barcode tag
options.rationale: Barcodes must be scanned close up.

options.content: A CNC controller
A magnetic stripe card
options.rationale: Cards are used for payments and access.

explanation: Tracking collars contain a GPS receiver and a transmitter.

stem: In CAD/CAM, what happens to the CAD design file?

options.content: It is printed on paper and given to the workers, who then cut each part by hand
It is deleted once the part has been drawn
options.rationale: The design is used to make the part.

options.content: It is converted into instructions that control CNC machines to make the part
options.rationale: Correct: design and manufacture are linked.

options.content: It is posted on a social network so that customers can approve it

explanation: CAM machines work directly from the CAD file.

stem: Which is a benefit of CAD over drawing by hand?

options.content: No training at all is needed to use the CAD software
CAD software and computers cost nothing
Designs can be changed and tested on screen before anything is made
options.rationale: Correct: mistakes are found early, saving materials.

options.content: CAD software makes the finished parts as well as designing them on screen

explanation: CAD drawings are accurate, easy to edit, viewable in 3D and testable by simulation.

stem: Which sensor is most important for the safety of miners working underground?

options.content: A light sensor fitted to the windows of the mine office
options.rationale: Not a safety sensor for miners.

options.content: A moisture sensor in a flower bed
A barcode reader used to record items in the mine's stores
A gas sensor detecting methane or carbon monoxide
options.rationale: Correct: dangerous gases must be detected early.

explanation: Gas, temperature and airflow sensors protect miners; the computer controls fans and alarms.

stem: In an ore-processing plant, a sensor shows that the pH in a tank is below the stored limit. What does the control computer do?

options.content: Switches off the pH sensor
Prints a report on the low pH reading for the manager to read next month
Increases the speed of the ore conveyor
options.rationale: Adding more ore does not correct the pH.

options.content: Signals a pump to add more lime until the pH is within limits
options.rationale: Correct: the actuator corrects the condition.

explanation: The computer compares readings with limits and signals actuators to correct them.
hints: Process control follows the read–compare–act cycle.

stem: Rangers want to detect poachers entering a park at night. Which system is most suitable?

options.content: A spreadsheet of the park's visitor bookings and permits
Thermal cameras and drones sending alerts to a control room
options.rationale: Correct: thermal imaging works in the dark.

options.content: A CAD drawing of the park fence
A tracking collar fitted to each of the rangers on patrol

explanation: Thermal cameras, camera traps, drones and acoustic sensors are used against poaching.
hints: Which technology detects people at night without light?

stem: Why must the location data from rhino tracking collars be kept secure?

options.content: The collars stop working if the data is shared
options.rationale: Sharing does not affect the collars.

options.content: Poachers could use it to find the rhinos
options.rationale: Correct: the data is valuable to criminals.

options.content: Tourists are not allowed to see rhinos
options.rationale: Tourists may see rhinos; the issue is criminals.

options.content: The data is too large to store on a computer

explanation: Location data must be protected by access controls and encryption.
hints: Who else would like to know where rhinos are?

stem: Computer-aided manufacturing uses computers to control machines such as CNC lathes and 3D printers.
A tracking collar on its own stops an elephant from entering farmland.
explanation: False. The collar only reports its position; rangers or farmers act on alerts.

stem: A lion's tracking collar sends its position every 30 minutes. How many positions does it send in one day?
Researchers fit the same type of collar (one position every 30 minutes) to 8 elephants. How many positions are stored in their database each day?
workedSolution:
1. One collar: 1440 ÷ 30 = 48 positions per day.
2. 8 collars: 48 × 8 = 384.
hints: Find the number for one collar first.

Drawing and testing a new pump design on screen
Cutting metal parts to exact sizes from a program

payload.template: Using computers to monitor and control an industrial process continuously is called process {{blank:a}}. A machine tool controlled by a program of exact co-ordinates is a {{blank:b}} machine.

stem: Give **two** benefits of using computers to control ore processing at a mine. [2]

points.description: Continuous, accurate control keeps each stage within limits / more mineral recovered, less waste
Fewer workers needed in dangerous areas / faster response / alarms when a value cannot be corrected

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Conditions are controlled continuously and accurately, so more gold is recovered, and fewer workers are exposed to dangerous chemicals.

hints: Think about safety and recovery of minerals.

stem: Describe how GPS tracking collars help reduce conflict between elephants and farmers near a national park. [4]

points.description: The collar's GPS receiver works out the elephant's position at regular intervals
The position is transmitted by satellite / mobile network to the park's computer
The computer shows the elephants on a map and sends an alert when one crosses a set boundary near farms (geofence)
Rangers / farmers are warned in time to move the elephants away / protect crops

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Each collar works out the elephant's position regularly and sends it to the park's computer. The computer plots it on a map and sends an alert when an elephant crosses a boundary near the farms, so rangers can drive it back before crops are damaged.

hints: Position → transmitted → computer map → alert → rangers act.

stem: Zambezi Metalworks (fictional) in Bulawayo is moving from hand drawing and manual lathes to CAD/CAM.

options.content: Parts are designed and tested on screen
Machines are controlled by computer to make the parts
Parts are checked by hand with a ruler and gauge
Customers' orders are taken by email

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe **three** benefits of CAD/CAM for the company.

points.description: Designs changed and tested on screen before making, so less waste
Faster production / machines work continuously / safer for workers

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Every part is made to exactly the same size; designs can be tested and corrected on screen, so less metal is wasted; and CNC machines work quickly and continuously.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Give **two** drawbacks for the company or its workers.

points.description: Workers need retraining / some manual jobs lost

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The equipment is expensive, and lathe operators must be retrained or may lose their jobs.

explanation: CAM makes, CAD designs; accuracy and speed against cost and jobs.

stem: A coal mine near Hwange uses computers to keep the air underground safe.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe how the computer system controls the ventilation.

points.description: Gas (methane / carbon monoxide) and airflow sensors take readings continuously
Readings are converted (ADC) and sent to the computer, which compares them with stored safe limits
If gas is above the limit, the computer signals the fans (actuators) to speed up / sounds an alarm

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Methane and airflow sensors take readings continuously; these are converted to digital and compared with the stored safe limits. If methane rises above its limit, the computer speeds up the ventilation fans and sounds an alarm. This repeats continuously.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Evaluate the system: give **one** benefit and **one** drawback.

points.description: Benefit: dangerous gas detected and cleared faster than by people / continuous monitoring saves lives
Drawback: dust / water damage sensors so faulty readings / expensive / power failure stops fans

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Gas is detected and cleared faster than any person could, saving lives; but dust and water can damage the sensors and give false readings.

explanation: Sensors, comparison with limits, fans and alarms, repeated; life-saving but sensors need maintenance.
hints: Name a sensor and an actuator.
